items.title: 61428_Red Callender oral history interview
items.q: In this group, we had a bassoon, tuba, clarinet, flute, and oboe. I played the tuba, of course, and James Newton played the flute and did most of the writing. John Carter, clarinet; I forgot to mention that.

ctx.x: We were playing Reel 2 back a minute ago, and at the point where I asked you on Reel 2 how you feel about the bass as opposed to the tuba, and you said you loved them equally, and when you listened to your response, you said off the tape that it depended on whom you were working with. I wanted to ask you now if you would amplify on that.

And I went on to say that it would depend... It always depends upon whom you're working with, I guess. Because last July, I took a trip to Europe with one of the wildest groups I've ever played with in my life, and I think I had more fun than I've ever had before playing the tuba with anybody.
